published.citation: Harrington et al. 2007, dayside brightness temperature at 8 µm (NASA Exoplanet Archive emission table): 2300 +/- 200 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007Natur.447..691H/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse at 8 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)) and nobody has imaged it, so the colour is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: 1 measured of 146 rows; the smallest relative uncertainty, then the longest wavelength
temperature.facility: Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)
